title: GPU + Kubernetes interop incident playbook and validation matrix (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This working draft captures a compact incident/playbook oriented approach to validating and rolling upgrades for on‑prem/VPC Kubernetes clusters running GPU workloads. Focus is on fast detection of driver/CUDA/NCCL regressions, safe canary waves, and short deterministic rollback paths. This is intended for SREs and private deployment engineers validating vendor driver updates, node image changes, or Kubernetes runtime upgrades that might affect inference latency or correctness.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: k8s clusters with NVIDIA GPUs (A100, A10, L4-like), containerd or docker runtime, workloads using contiguous streaming inference and KV cache.
- Assumes access to cluster admin (kubeconfig with cluster-admin), image registry, and onprem hardware console.
- This doc complements the broader compatibility matrix (canonical matrix lives in Confluence link above) with pragmatic verification steps and incident response actions.

High-level goals:
1) Detect functional regressions (OOMs, NCCL timeouts, kernel panics) quickly in canary wave.
2) Detect performance regressions (per-token latency p50/p99 increases) within 30 minutes of rollout.
3) Provide deterministic rollback play to previous node-image/driver/CRI state.

Quick glossary (short):
- Node-image: OS + kernel + vendor packages used for GPU nodes.
- Driver: NVIDIA Linux driver package version (e.g., 535.113).
- CUDA: CUDA toolkit version available to containers (libcudart visible).
- NCCL: NCCL lib used by inference stacks for collectives or GPU comms (often used by perf tests).
- CRI: container runtime interface (containerd or dockerd).

Pre-upgrade checklist (gates):
- Backup cluster autoscaler and any custom node pools config (terraform state snapshot).
- Snapshot current node-image AMIs/OVAs.
- Record current cluster-level metrics (past 24h) for latency, token throughput, pod OOMs, kernel OOPS, ECC errors.
- Lock model-serving image tags to digest for the rollout window.
- Create canary node pool (min size 1, max size 3) with taints: gpu-rollout=true:NoSchedule.

Validation probes (scripts to run, lightweight):
1) driver-probe.sh (run on node): checks nvidia-smi, driver module, kernel log for NVidia messages, verifies MIG visibility. Output: PASS/FAIL + short diagnostics.
2) cuda-probe-container (container image: redwood/gpu-probes:smoke): runs small matrix-mul, allocates 2GB GPU memory, runs cudaMemcpy and reports runtime and any cuda errors. Exit code non-zero on failure.
3) nccl-ringtest (container): run NCCL tests at 1-rank and multi-rank (if >1 GPU) to catch mislinked NCCL symbols or runtime ABI failures.
4) perf-token-sim (local client): sends steady stream of short prompts to canary pods and measures p50/p99 and error rate for 15 minutes.

Compatibility/Validation matrix (condensed view used for quick checks):
Columns: node_os | kernel | k8s | CRI | nvidia_driver | cuda | nccl | expected_notes
- ubuntu-22.04 | 5.15.0-86 | 1.27.x | containerd 1.7 | 535.86 | 12.1 | 2.17 | baseline, passes ringtest on A100
- ubuntu-22.04 | 5.19.0-46 | 1.28.x | containerd 1.7 | 550.14 | 12.2 | 2.18 | observed slightly higher p99 on L4 with 550
- rhel-8.8 | 4.18.0-516.el8 | 1.27.x | docker 20.10 | 535.113 | 11.8 | 2.14 | requires kernel param iommu=pt for MIG stability
- ubuntu-22.04 | 6.1.0-28 | 1.29-beta | containerd 1.8 | 565.10 | 12.3 | 2.19 | experimental k8s combo, run extended perf tests
Notes: This condensed matrix is intended to drive test selection. Always escalate to the canonical matrix if combination not listed here.

Canary rollout plan (recommended wave approach):
- Wave 0 (lab): 1 node in isolated lab cluster; run all probes.
- Wave 1 (canary pool): 1-3 nodes, tainted and labeled for traffic split (10% of traffic routed to canary topology). Run smoke + perf-token-sim for 30 minutes.
- Wave 2 (progressive): Expand to 10% of production GPU capacity, hold for 2 hours, automated monitors gate (p99 increase >15% or error rate >1% triggers halt).
- Wave 3 (full): Drain/cordon, replace remaining nodes. Monitor 24h.

Automated monitoring gates (SLOs and thresholds):
- Latency: p99 token latency increase > 15% vs baseline -> auto-halt.
- Error rate: 5xx responses or CUDA failures > 1% -> auto-halt.
- Pod restarts/OOMs: any OOMKills on canary GPU pods -> auto-halt and collect logs.
- Node-level: ECC correctable errors > 50 within 1h or any GPU ECC uncorrectable -> emergency rollback.

Immediate incident response (if a gate trips):
1) Halt rollout in pipeline; mark terraform apply as paused.
2) Add annotation to canary pool nodes: incident/blocked-by=<reason>.
3) Execute rollback play: scale up previous node pool (with driver version pinned), cordon & drain new nodes from service, and migrate traffic back.
4) Collect artifacts: dmesg, /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, container logs, kernel OOPS snippets, pod core dumps (if any). Upload to incident blobstore (link in linked artifacts).
5) Open a postmortem ticket and tag devs:driver-team + eng-private-deployments.

Rollback recipe (deterministic):
- Preconditions: previous node-image AMI available, terraform state with previous labels.
- Steps: terraform apply using pinned node_pool.image_digest set to previous digest -> scale to same capacity as production -> drain replacement nodes and ensure app pods schedule on rolled-back nodes -> run perf-token-sim to validate.
- Time estimate: 20–45 minutes for small clusters; depends on node spin-up time.

Post-incident validation checklist (after rollback):
- Confirm p50/p99 back to baseline in 30 minutes.
- Confirm no new kernel OOPS in 2 hours.
- Archive failing artifacts and label with experiment metadata (driver, cuda, node-image digest, k8s version).

Edge cases and gotchas observed in lab (learning notes):
- Mixed driver versions on same cluster can hide failures until pods land on problematic nodes; use node labels to avoid mixing during rollout.
- containerd versions with specific snapshotters can change latency characteristics for cold-starts; test cold-start median separately.
- NCCL ABI mismatches often surfaced as subtle hangs (no explicit error), so include short kill-timeouts for ringtest jobs to detect hangs.
- Some vendor installers replace kernel modules in-place causing node to need reboot; include a preflight check that ensures reboot not required or schedule maintenance window.

Smoke tests (to run automatically post-provision):
- node-smoke: runs driver-probe.sh, checks GPUs visible, MIG counts if configured, and disk IO.
- container-smoke: runs redwood/gpu-probes:smoke to exercise cudaMalloc + cuBLAS simple ops.
- inference-smoke: launches a single-replica of model server with 1 request/sec for 5 minutes validating outputs not degraded (hash comparison on deterministic outputs).

Observability and data collection (what to capture):
- kube-events, pod logs, containerd logs, dmesg, metrics from node exporter (gpu temp, memory), nvidia-smi samples every 10s during canary window, NCCL debug logs if enabled.
- Retain artifacts with tag: rollout-<date>-<driver> for 7d before moving to cold storage.

Runbook snippets (commands):
- Check nvidia modules on node: ssh node && sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 10
- Basic cuda probe: kubectl run cuda-probe --image=redwood/gpu-probes:smoke --restart=Never -- /bin/sh -c "./cuda-smoke.sh"
- Collect logs for pod: kubectl logs <pod> -n model-serving --previous > /tmp/pod.log

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing playbook):
- Should we standardize on containerd snapshotter X for all node-pools? (tradeoffs: snapshot speed vs stability)
- Minimum automation to perform full rollback without manual terraform edits? (owner: platform-eng)
- How to integrate NCCL verbose logs into the centralized observability without overwhelming token budget?

Action items (owners):
- (Ava) Draft small Jenkins pipeline step for canary gating with automated perf-token-sim.
- (Ravi) Build driver-probe.sh into redwood/gpu-probes image and publish tags.
- (Maya) Wireup automated artifact upload to private blobstore on gate failure.

Appendix: Suggested short test sequence for any driver update:
1) lab-provision -> run node-smoke + cuda-probe + nccl-ringtest
2) wave1 canary -> run inference-smoke + perf-token-sim (30m)
3) run extended perf (2h) on 10% capacity
4) roll if all gates pass

End of draft.

Notes: This document is deliberately compact and operational; it is a working artifact and will be expanded with links to concrete scripts and terraform snippets once owners complete tasks above.
